messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: canary-rollout v4.2.0 p99 latency > 2.5s across streaming endpoints (auto-paged). Link: https://dashboard.redwood/alerts/1877773333 :rotating_light:

michael-oncall: saw it. paging now. i'm oncall, grabbing logs and tracing.

michael-oncall: p95 ~ 400ms, p99 ~ 3.2s on /v1/stream; spike aligns with traffic shift to canary (5%->30%) at 14:03 UTC.

sara-platform: copying — can we confirm whether this is tail latency (single-host) or distributed? dash shows high tail on a subset of hosts in ash-region.

diane-sre: digging into host list: 3 hosts with p99 > 6s, rest fine. KV cache evictions high on those nodes. possible memory pressure during long-stream sessions.

michael-oncall: streaming stalls observed: clients get partial tokens then stall for 4-10s before resume. stacktrace shows heavy GC on python side in that runtime.

llm-infra: that's the new fp16 quant path we rolled with v4.2.0 — kernel change + new batching behavior. Any chance of a regression?

sara-platform: we pushed canary at 14:00, traffic ramp policy hit 30% at 14:03. quick check: kernel selector preferred 'quant-path-v2' on those hosts.

diane-sre: mitigation options: 1) rollback canary to previous model variant 2) route canary traffic to different pool 3) throttle canary traffic to 5% immediate. Which to attempt first?

michael-oncall: priority = restore SLO for customers. prefer option 3 then 1 if needed. throttle to 5% now. @sara-platform can you push traffic policy?

sara-platform: doing now — lowering canary to 5% (policy: traffic.set canary=0.05). ETA ~ 30s.

ops-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: canary traffic adjusted to 5% by sara-platform at 14:12:22 UTC.

julia-support: flagging top customers with streaming sessions >30s; we'll notify SRE if any 500s or client-visible errors. So far only latency, no errors.

michael-oncall: after throttle, p99 dropped to 1.1s in ~1m. looks like load-sensitive tail. continuing to monitor for 10m.

llm-infra: let's not push a full rollback yet. We'll collect core dumps and kernel logs from the three offending hosts. sara, can you pin a sampling trace for requests hitting the quant-path-v2?

sara-platform: sampling traces enabled (5% sampling) and archive started. core dumps request open for host ids host-ash-12/13/14. /eng-infra runbook linked: https://playbook.redwood/streaming-tail-debug

diane-sre: found process OOM-like churn: python worker cycles heavy mem alloc/free during KV cache refill. quant-path-v2 increased memory working set by ~30% under long sequences.

michael-oncall: next steps: (A) keep canary at 5% (B) collect artifacts for rollback decision (C) schedule a rapid rollback if we see re-escalation. I'll handoff to night oncall in 25m — leaving monitoring dashboards and runbook notes.

julia-support: prepping customer comms: no customer errors yet, but degraded latency for some streaming sessions. will notify customers on affected SLAs if this persists >30m.

ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigation (throttle) successful; p99 back under SLO. Monitoring window in place until 14:45 UTC.

diane-sre: if p99 creeps up again, we should rollback to v4.1.7 variant-by-default. I can coordinate the rollback; need +/- 5m for safe cutover.

michael-oncall: thanks — i'll leave a handoff note: handoff-to=diane-sre at 14:30 UTC. if you take over, please run rollback playbook only after confirming artifacts and coordinator signoff.

sara-platform: added runbook note + links to traces and kernels in the incident channel.

michael-oncall: wrapping up: incident severity -> P1 alert (potential SLO breach). mitigation: throttle to 5% immediate. current status: monitoring, customer impact limited to increased streaming tail latency for small subset. handoff to diane in 25m.

diane-sre: acknowledged. I'll be on standby and will escalate to rollback if p99 > 2s for next 10m on >2 hosts. :thumbsup:
